clue.text: A revolutionary plan going round the educational community

parts.note: Jack Cade led a fifteenth-century rebellion in England, so a revolutionary

indicators.note: going round means the word for plan is turned back to front

parts.note: to aim is to plan or intend

explanation.surface: A radical scheme circulating among academics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' reverses the plan word. Jack Cade led a rebellion against Henry VI in 1450, a stock crossword revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the world of universities and scholars, a learned community.

clue.text: Diamonds are real, asked initially? Sauce!

parts.note: diamonds are pure crystalline carbon

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the words that come before

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether diamonds are genuine and gets cheek in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce!' looks like an exclamation at cheek but is the pasta dish's sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbonara is an Italian pasta sauce of egg, cheese and bacon.

clue.text: Suffering from a number of blows

definitions.text: Suffering from a number of blows

parts.words: Suffering from a number of blows
parts.note: a numb limb after being struck on the thigh; 'number' hints at numbness

explanation.definitionFit: A dead leg is the numbness in a thigh after a blow to the muscle.

clue.text: Cheeky madam finally moves to the front in panic

indicators.note: the named letter goes from its place to the start of the panic word

parts.note: alarm is panic or fright

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: A rude woman pushes to the head of a frightened crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' picks M from madam; 'moves to the front in' takes the M of ALARM to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Malar is an anatomical adjective meaning of the cheek or cheekbone.

clue.text: Article written on British diver

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
UK, the United Kingdom, stands for British

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a British swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'written on' places A above UK.
explanation.definitionFit: The auk is a seabird that dives underwater to catch fish.

clue.text: So-called person beating the booze

indicators.note: so-called signals a word that is said, giving a soundalike

parts.note: one who licks an opponent, beating them, is a licker

explanation.surface: A man said to be thrashing someone over drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So-called' points to how the word sounds: LICKER said aloud matches the spelling of strong drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquor is alcoholic drink, especially spirits, the same as booze.

clue.text: His policy: carrying one to bed when husband's away?

definitions.text: His policy: carrying one to bed when husband's away?

indicators.note: carrying means the policy word holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: a line is a policy, as in the party line
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: away says the husband letter is missing from the bed word

parts.note: a berth is a bed on a ship or train
H is short for husband

explanation.surface: A rake's tactic is to bed women while their husbands are out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' and 'when husband's away' are the indicators; the whole clue also describes a seducer, so it is an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: A libertine is a dissolute man who seduces freely, exactly the conduct the clue describes.

clue.text: Somewhere to live down south for three months

indicators.note: down means lacking, so the south letter is removed

parts.note: quarters are lodgings, somewhere to live

explanation.surface: Moving to a place in the south for a season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down south' reads as heading south but means short of S.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter of the year spans three months.

clue.text: Duck is able to cross Eastern Pacific

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

indicators.note: the able word crosses, so it holds the eastern letter inside it

parts.note: can means is able

explanation.surface: A duck manages to swim across the eastern Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific is the largest of the world's oceans.

clue.text: Characters involved in Shakespearean plot

indicators.note: the letters (characters) sitting inside the next word supply the run

explanation.surface: Figures caught up in the story of a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters involved in' says the answer's letters are found within ShakespEAREAn.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot of land is an area, a piece of ground.

clue.text: What pyromaniac must do furiously

definitions.meaning: a fire-raiser has a liking for fires, read literally
an idiom for doing something with great vigour

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very fast or intensely, and read literally it says fancying fires.

clue.text: Very, very good standard not welcomed in the main

definitions.text: standard not welcomed in the main

parts.note: jolly is British informal for very
roger is radio slang for message received, very good

explanation.surface: A top-quality flag nobody at sea is happy to see.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is the open sea; a standard is a flag, here the pirates' skull and crossbones.
explanation.definitionFit: The pirate flag was an unwelcome banner on the high seas, as sailors feared pirates.

clue.text: See red after game's over

parts.note: Go is an Asian board game
spare means left over or surplus

explanation.surface: Losing one's temper once the match is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: GO SPARE is British slang for becoming furious.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red and to go spare are both idioms for flying into a rage.

clue.text: Give spanking good smack

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to give them a beating

explanation.surface: A tasty spanking delivered with a slap.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack is a distinctive flavour, a sharp taste, as in a smack of garlic.

clue.text: Pain and misfortune - - yet one remains optimistic

parts.note: a pang is a sudden sharp pain
a loss is a misfortune or setback

explanation.surface: Despite suffering and setbacks, someone stays hopeful.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Pangloss, in Voltaire's Candide, insists that all is for the best in the best of all possible worlds.
explanation.definitionFit: Pangloss is the literary byword for an incurable optimist despite every disaster.

clue.text: Tell me quickly what's unfashionable and fashion able!

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
with it means up to date, fashionable

explanation.surface: Asking someone to say quickly what is out of style and what is in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion able' is split to be read as fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation urges someone to speak up without delay.

clue.text: Offensive radio broadcast about noon

indicators.note: about places the rearranged letters around the single letter for noon
broadcast means the letters of the word are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: An insulting radio programme aired around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns RADIO into IROAD, and 'about' puts it round N to give I-N-ROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: An inroad is an incursion or raid, an offensive push into territory.

clue.text: A welcome home for chaps in union

indicators.note: the welcome word acts as a home, so the chaps go inside it

parts.note: to greet is to welcome
men are chaps

explanation.surface: A friendly reception at a men's hostel in a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home for' is the container indicator: the welcome houses the chaps, and 'union' means accord, not a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: An agreement is a union of minds, an accord between parties.

clue.text: Dash outside with criminal

indicators.note: outside means the first word's letters go around the second's

parts.note: a dash of something is a bit
and means together with

explanation.surface: Rushing out of doors with a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash' looks like a verb of hurrying but means a small amount, BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is an outlaw or robber, a criminal.

clue.text: Striking as blade might be

definitions.meaning: a blade is a ... young man, and a blade is also something ... (swishing)

explanation.definitionFit: The word means stylishly attractive, and a blade is old slang for a dashing young man.

clue.text: What may be drunk by a politician is dependent on chance

parts.note: ale is a drink
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Whether a politician gets drunk is a matter of luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleatory comes from the Latin for dice and means depending on luck or random events.

clue.text: A Catherine that had Sinatra smitten?

indicators.note: smitten, struck hard, means the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A Russian empress who swooned over the crooner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smitten' rearranges SINATRA; Catherine the Great was a Russian empress.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine the Great was a tsarina, a Russian empress.

clue.text: Successfully secures a great deal

definitions.meaning: to claim or grab something first
plenty, as in having lots of time

explanation.definitionFit: To claim something is to get hold of it; lots of something can be described informally as heaps.

clue.text: Saying of Lovelace, say, has turned up

parts.note: Ada Lovelace was the nineteenth-century mathematician

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A remark by the mathematician has come to light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses EG to GE.
explanation.definitionFit: An adage is a proverb or saying.

clue.text: Craft needed by person with failing party?

definitions.text: Craft needed by person with failing party?

parts.words: Craft needed by person with failing party?
parts.note: craft reads as a skill, but it is also a vessel that clears frozen sea; a flat party needs something to loosen the guests

explanation.definitionFit: The term names both a ship that breaks through ice and an opening remark that eases social stiffness.

clue.text: Upsetting salt over turkey wings could make one cross

indicators.note: over puts the first piece above the second in a down clue
in a down clue upsetting turns the word upside down, so backwards

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, an old salt

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Spilling salt on the turkey would annoy anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upsetting' turns TAR into RAT; 'wings' gives T and Y from turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British informal for irritable or bad-tempered.

clue.text: Ecstasy obtained from him servant adulterated

indicators.note: adulterated means corrupted, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Rapture gained from a servant who has been corrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adulterated' rearranges HIM SERVANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravishment is a state of rapture or delight, a sense of being transported.

clue.text: Fish given in list (after horse)

indicators.note: after the horse has gone, so the horse letter is removed

parts.note: a ship lists or heels when it leans over
horse is slang for heroin, H

explanation.surface: A fish served in a list after the horse course.
explanation.walkthrough: '(after horse)' reads as horse gone: H leaves HEEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An eel is a long snakelike fish.

clue.text: Romantic couple's bit of news

definitions.meaning: two people who are dating, a pair

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a dating pair and a single piece in a newspaper or bulletin.

clue.text: Crowning moment of the second of Three Men In A Boat

indicators.note: the second letter of the following word is selected

parts.note: a rowing eight is a racing boat crewed by eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: The best moment of a famous comic novel's second part.
explanation.walkthrough: Three Men in a Boat is a Jerome K Jerome novel; here the title splits into the second letter of 'Three' and a rowing crew.
explanation.definitionFit: The height of something is its peak or climax, the crowning point.

clue.text: Ruin song with one dance move that's not quiet

parts.note: a lay is a ballad or song
A means one

indicators.note: says the letter for quiet is absent from the dance move

parts.note: a step is a dance move
P stands for piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: Wrecking a song by adding a noisy dance routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's not quiet' removes P from STEP, leaving STE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay waste is to devastate or destroy a place, ruin it utterly.
